_comment: Tier-2 for skfem time_dependent#2, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 / scipy 1.15.3. Claim: factor the time-stepping matrix once with scipy.sparse.linalg.factorized() and reuse it; the signal given is a PROFILE showing >90% of time in spsolve. This fixture deliberately asserts nothing about wall-clock -- timing assertions go red on a busy machine -- and checks the claim structurally instead. Ran: heat equation on a 32x32 MeshTri.init_tensor with ElementTriP1 (1089 DOFs, 7361 non-zeros; condensed 961x961 with 6481 non-zeros), backward Euler, 20 steps, once through skfem.solve/condense and once through a single factorized() callable, with scipy.sparse.linalg.spsolve and scipy.sparse.linalg._dsolve.linsolve.splu wrapped by counters. Printed: the matrix has ZERO differing non-zeros between steps, so reuse is legal; the naive loop calls spsolve 20 times (once per step) and the factorized loop calls it 0 times; factorized performs EXACTLY ONE LU; and a counter on splu alone reports 0 for the spsolve loop because spsolve calls SuperLU directly, so splu alone would prove nothing. The two loops agree to 7.772e-16. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 applies the documented fix to the naive first loop, which then factors Ac once with scipy.sparse.linalg.factorized() and calls the returned lu_fixed per step instead of solve(*condense(A, M @ u, D=D)). Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 11 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'spsolve_loop_spsolve_calls=20', 'spsolve_called_once_per_step=True' and 'splu_counter_alone_is_blind_to_spsolve=True' (and emits 'FAIL:'), so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
